name: Anterolateral approach to the proximal tibia (periprosthetic knee)
corridor: Anterolateral window through fascia anterior to the iliotibial tract, releasing tibialis anterior from the lateral tibia without periosteal stripping, optionally using a prior midline TKA incision or a more lateral mini-incision

positioning.text: Position so the prior midline scar, Gerdy tubercle, and lateral tibial crest can be seen and the knee imaged.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the prior midline TKA incision, Gerdy tubercle, and the anterior tibial crest. A more lateral mini-incision is chosen if the sentinel scar is too medial.

incision.text: Reuse the midline TKA incision when it allows safe retraction. If it is too medial, make a more lateral minimally invasive cut. Skin risk is lower when the fracture is remote from the arthroplasty.

superficial_interval.text: Open deep fascia anterior to the iliotibial tract. Release the proximal tibialis anterior attachment, and if needed incise the IT band or take a small Gerdy flake.

deep_interval.text: Elevate tibialis anterior from bone without stripping periosteum and retract it laterally. Do not chase the posteromedial tibia from this side.

layers.text: Skin (prior midline or new lateral), fascia and IT band, tibialis anterior, periosteum, then the lateral proximal tibia.

structures_at_risk.text: The extensor mechanism and the skin bridge between a medial TKA scar and a new lateral cut are at risk. Posteromedial dissection from this side is hazardous.

danger_zones.text: Do not expose the posteromedial tibia from anterolateral. That risks the extensor mechanism and a poorly healing skin envelope.

retraction_hazards.text: Judge how much retraction a reused midline scar can tolerate before making a separate lateral window.

exposure.text: Shows the lateral proximal tibia for periprosthetic plating without a formal submeniscal plateau reconstruction unless the adult extensile window is added.

limitations.text: Posteromedial fragments cannot be reached. A too-medial TKA scar may force a second lateral incision.

indications.text: Used for anterolateral fixation of a proximal-tibial periprosthetic fracture around a total knee.

closure.text: Irrigate the joint if it was opened, close in layers, consider a drain, and close skin with staples or nonabsorbable suture.

complications.text: Complications include skin-bridge necrosis between a reused midline scar and a new lateral cut, and extensor-mechanism injury from posteromedial dissection.

procedure_applications.condition: A proximal-tibial periprosthetic fracture is plated from anterolateral, respecting a prior midline TKA scar

questions.question: When is a new lateral mini-incision preferred over the TKA scar?
questions.answer: When the sentinel midline incision is too medial to allow safe visualization without excessive retraction.

questions.question: Why must posteromedial tibia not be exposed from this side?
questions.answer: It risks the extensor mechanism and creates a difficult skin-healing environment.

questions.question: How is tibialis anterior handled?
questions.answer: Released from bone without periosteal stripping and retracted laterally.
